Kind regards,
[Your name]

Subject: Repainting the living room before I move out

Hi Orla,

I hope you're well. As my move-out date of 30 June is coming up, I wanted to check something with you.

Would you be happy for me to repaint the living room walls on the weekend before I leave? I'd use the original pale grey so everything matches, and I'd take care to cover the floors and skirting properly and leave the room clean and tidy afterwards.

I know your decorator is booked for 2 July, so please don't feel you need to say yes — I just wanted to offer, as I'd like to hand the place back looking cared for. If you'd rather I left the walls as they are for the decorator, that's completely fine too.

Thanks very much, and let me know what you'd prefer.

Best wishes,
[Your name]

Note: Since Orla's decorator will repaint the whole living room on 2 July at her expense regardless of its condition, your repainting would likely be redundant — you may want to save the time and money and instead just leave the room clean and ask whether she'd like anything else done.

Dear Ms Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June for the flat I rented from you.

I moved out and removed all of my belongings on 31 May, and the flat was empty from that date onwards. Because I was unable to get to your office until 8 June, that was the first day I could hand back the keys.

I understand that our agreement states rent continues until all keys are returned, so I recognise the charge for 1 to 8 June reflects the terms we both signed. Nonetheless, as I was not living in or using the flat at any point in June, I would be very grateful if you would consider refunding the rent charged for those eight days as a gesture of goodwill.

If you are able to agree, please send the refund to my usual account. I am happy to confirm the details if needed.

Thank you for your time and for your consideration.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Your new address]
[Phone / email]

Dear Ms. Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent charged to me for 1 to 8 June.

As you know, I removed all of my belongings from the flat on 31 May and was not living there at any point in June. I was only unable to return the keys until 8 June, as that was the first day I could get to your office.

While I understand that our signed agreement states rent continues through the day all keys are returned, I would like to respectfully request a refund of the rent charged for 1 to 8 June, given that the flat was empty and I was not occupying it during that period.

I would be grateful if you could send the refund to my usual account.

Thank you very much for your consideration. Please let me know if you need anything further from me.

Kind regards,
[Your name]

Note: Since your agreement says rent runs until keys are returned, she may be entitled to keep the 1–8 June charge, so the letter frames this as a goodwill request.
